approved: Governor-General Amendment (Cessation of Allowances in the Public Interest) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would stop paying allowances to former Governors-General or their spouses who have engaged in serious misconduct.
The Minister could declare through a legislative instrument that payments cease, or a House of Parliament could pass a resolution to stop them.
The bill fills a gap in the Governor-General Act 1974, which currently requires allowances to be paid even after a criminal conviction.
Allowances can be stopped for serious misconduct via a ministerial legislative instrument.
Allowances can be stopped for serious misconduct via a resolution of a House of Parliament.
The bill adds a public interest test to the Governor-General Act 1974.
